name: full-corpus-reproduction
title: Full BioModels reproduction across all simulators (1008 models × 5 engines)
claim: Running the full BioModels corpus through the batch-compare-biomodels composite under up to five independent ODE engines reproduces 1008 models (14.7M timecourse rows) at corpus scale: 306 models are covered by all five engines and 725 by four or more. This study establishes COVERAGE — how broadly each model is cross-run and that the per-model, per-engine trajectories are committed and browsable model-by-model in the corpus explorer. Scored trajectory AGREEMENT against the BioSimulators reference is measured in the sibling repeat-matching study (currently on the BIOMD1-3 validation subset), not quantified corpus-wide here.
question: Across the entire BioModels corpus, do independent simulators (COPASI, Tellurium, simbio, AMICI, PySCeS) reproduce the same trajectories, and where do they diverge?
hypothesis: Standards-based SBML/SED-ML models integrate to the same solution regardless of engine; systematic disagreement flags a model-encoding ambiguity or an engine-specific numerical behaviour.
objective: Fetch and parse every BioModel, run each through every available simulator via the batch-compare-biomodels composite (fanned out over the corpus with the Ray runner), and record the full per-model, per-engine, per-variable timecourse as a single tidy dataset for cross-engine comparison.
description: This is the full-corpus reproduction run. The batch-compare-biomodels composite fetches each model's SBML, parses every SED-ML simulation, runs each engine over all jobs, and reports all-pairs nRMSE per (model, SED-ML doc). Executed over the whole corpus with viva_biomodels.ray_runner (one Ray task per model, crash-isolated). The result — 1008 models, up to five engines each, 14.7M rows — is committed at datasets/corpus_all_engines/ (a sorted tidy parquet + a compact per-model index.json) and served to the corpus explorer (Analyses tab) as one JSON per model for lazy, model-by-model browsing.
readouts: n_models — BioModels reproduced across at least one engine (=1008)
n_models_ge_4_engines — models covered by four or more engines (=725)
n_models_5_engines — models covered by all five engines (=306)
per_engine_coverage — models each engine simulated (tellurium 985, amici 879, copasi 870, pysces 770, simbio 367)

variants.name: full-corpus-sweep
variants.diff_from_baseline: Fan the per-model baseline composite over every BioModel id (biomodels.get_all_identifiers()) via the Ray runner; the committed dataset is the union of all per-model results.

expected_behavior.name: corpus-coverage-full
expected_behavior.rationale: The reproduction must span the corpus, not a token subset. 1008 models were fetched, parsed, and simulated.

expected_behavior.name: multi-engine-cross-check
expected_behavior.rationale: A genuine cross-engine reproduction needs most models covered by several independent engines. 725 models have >=4 engines and 306 have all five.

canonical_runs.name: full-corpus
canonical_runs.description: The full corpus sweep over all BioModels across all five engines, executed via viva_biomodels.ray_runner. Result committed at datasets/corpus_all_engines/ (tidy parquet + per-model index).

findings.statement: Corpus-scale reproduction is feasible and repeatable: 1008 BioModels were fetched, parsed and simulated under up to five independent ODE engines (14.7M timecourse rows), committed as one tidy parquet + per-model index.

Coverage is broad, not a two-engine spot check: 306 models carry all five engines and 725 carry four or more. Per-engine reach is uneven — tellurium 985, amici 879, copasi 870, pysces 770, simbio 367 — so simbio is the coverage-limiting engine, not a correctness-limiting one.
findings.next_action: Investigate why simbio covers fewer models (parse/feature gaps) to raise five-engine coverage above 306.

findings.statement: This study measures COVERAGE, not scored trajectory agreement. Whether the overlapping engines actually agree per-model is inspectable in the corpus explorer and quantified on the BIOMD1-3 subset by the repeat-matching study (exact agreement where observables are computed). The corpus-wide agreement claim is therefore scoped — supported by the subset result plus per-model explorability, not yet a corpus-wide scored number.
findings.next_action: Run the repeat-/reproducibility-match scorer across the full corpus against the BioSimulators reference to replace explorability with a corpus-wide agreement statistic.

regression_compatibility.basis: The Ray fan-out completed corpus-wide (crash-isolated per model); the committed parquet + index are the reproducible artifact.

biological_validation.basis: Both coverage gates pass (n_models >= 1000; n_models_ge_4_engines >= 700). These certify corpus-scale coverage; scored agreement is the sibling study's gate, not this one's.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-03 draws the line between coverage (established here) and scored agreement (repeat-matching), preventing the common overclaim that broad coverage equals demonstrated cross-engine agreement.

conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_pass: Corpus-scale coverage is established — 1008 models reproduced under up to five engines, 725 with four or more — and committed as a reusable dataset plus a per-model explorer. Proceed to quantify scored cross-engine agreement corpus-wide via the repeat-matching harness.
conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_fail: Coverage below the corpus threshold would mean the fetch/parse/simulate pipeline is dropping models; triage the Ray failures per model before making any reproduction claim.

limitations:
This study certifies COVERAGE, not scored trajectory agreement. Corpus-wide agreement against the BioSimulators reference is not quantified here — see repeat-matching (BIOMD1-3 subset) and the corpus explorer for per-model agreement.
Per-engine coverage is uneven; simbio (367/1008) limits five-engine coverage.
Single deterministic sweep (seed 0); the robustness axis is model/engine coverage, not seeds.
falsifiability: A corpus-wide repeat-/reproducibility-match run that found systematic numerical disagreement among the overlapping engines (beyond the understood coverage gaps) would overturn the implicit "the corpus reproduces" reading of this coverage result.
